articles.title: Prince William ‘blindsided’ by Harry, Meghan return as Kate fears new turmoil from royal feud: experts
articles.summary: Prince William was reportedly "blindsided" by the Sussexes' U.K. return, with royal experts saying he and Princess Catherine are concerned about the fallout.
articles.body: Prince William was reportedly "blindsided" by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s surprise decision to return to the U.K. with their children. Several royal experts told Fox News Digital that the Prince and Princess of Wales are "concerned" about the Duke and Duchess of Sussex returning for an extended period beginning this month. Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are set to begin school there in September, People magazine reported. "Prince William was blindsided," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY "He had found Harry’s recent eagerness to publicly signal that he wanted to spend more time in Britain unusual, but that is very different from anticipating a full return. William now has to navigate a situation he did not create, did not ask for and, given the state of their relationship, almost certainly would not have chosen." Fox News Digital reached out to Kensington Palace for comment. In a statement shared with The New York Times, a spokesperson for the Sussexes said, "On the heels of a wonderful trip with family and friends this summer, Harry and Meghan have decided to spend an extended period in the U.K. this autumn. They are excited to have their children spend more time in the country that’s such an important part of their family’s story." The spokesperson confirmed that the couple’s businesses will remain unchanged and based in the U.S. Meghan and Harry will also keep their home in California. British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that the Waleses are "feeling uneasy" about facing another chapter in the "endless Sussex soap opera." WATCH: PRINCE WILLIAM UNLIKELY TO RECONCILE WITH PRINCE HARRY SOON: EXPERT "It’s about broken trust," Chard explained. "Prince William is said to feel that Harry and Meghan have spent years attacking the institution, then monetizing their grievances through a very lucrative media operation. From his view, it’s an ongoing campaign for maximum impact and self-gain. He’s not going to fuel it, and he’s not going to endorse behavior he sees as damaging." William and Kate were seen arriving in Scotland on Thursday, where they’ll spend time with King Charles at Balmoral Castle. The royal family has spent summers at the Scottish estate since the reign of Queen Victoria, with family members traditionally hunting, fishing and horseback riding there. The king learned about Harry and Meghan’s move three days before it was made public, according to reports. "Prince William, along with Catherine, is currently at Balmoral Castle visiting the king," royal broadcaster Neil Sean told Fox News Digital. "Harry and Meghan have, so far, not been invited to visit the king privately while on a holiday. This will not happen while William is there. I’ve been told he has no desire to connect on any level with his younger brother and simply has no time for [Meghan]." Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell, which handles the offices of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, for comment. The Daily Mail reported that the king and his heir held a "Sussex Summit" following the announcement. A source told the outlet that the Prince and Princess of Wales "have no interest in engaging with anything Harry and Meghan do or say." Princess Catherine is particularly guarded given how deeply hurt she was by both of them. Both she and Prince William are very determined to maintain their own family stability and remain focused on duty with their royal roles paramount." Several royal experts previously told Fox News Digital that William and Harry haven’t been on speaking terms since at least 2022. "My sources have described genuine concern within the Wales camp," Schofield said. "I don’t think Prince William and Princess Catherine are sitting at Balmoral panicking about Harry and Meghan returning, but they are understandably apprehensive about what their return could bring. The last several years have taught them that private family tensions have a habit of becoming very public." "The concern isn’t simply that Harry and Meghan will be geographically closer," Schofield continued. "It’s the unpredictability that comes with the Sussexes. There have been interviews, books, documentaries and very personal allegations about members of the royal family. … My sources tell me the Wales camp has not forgotten the hostility directed at them after some of Harry and Meghan’s previous public accusations." Schofield said unnamed sources told her Kate is also unsettled by the news. "My sources tell me that Catherine does not want to revisit that chapter of her life," Schofield explained. My understanding has always been that her priority is Prince William, their children and the future." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? Too much has happened, and too much has been lost." The Sussexes are expected to live at a private, nonroyal residence outside London, The Associated Press reported. They won’t resume their royal duties, which they gave up in 2020. The couple’s return to the U.K. comes as the king continues treatment for an undisclosed form of cancer diagnosed in 2024. In 2025, Harry said he didn’t know "how much longer my father has" and expressed a desire for his children to get to know their grandfather. Last month, the king met with Harry, Meghan and their children at Highgrove House. Vanity Fair royal correspondent Katie Nicholl reported at the time that, according to sources, "not even the Prince and Princess of Wales were made aware that the meeting was taking place." articles.title: Sonam Kapoor REACTS to notices issued to 722 Mumbai auto and taxi drivers over Marathi language test
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing row over Maharashtra's new rule making Marathi mandatory for commercial vehicle drivers, actress Sonam Kapoor has reacted to the cont.
articles.body: Amid the ongoing row over Maharashtra's new rule making Marathi mandatory for commercial vehicle drivers, actress Sonam Kapoor has reacted to the controversy on social media. Her response comes as transport officials continue assessing drivers across Mumbai and the surrounding region, with hundreds found unable to speak the language. Let's learn more about it.Sonam Kapoor's reactionReacting to the development, Sonam Kapoor commented on a post by a journalist, simply writing, "Huh."What the transport assessment foundSince August 20, transport officials have assessed 5,211 drivers, including 3,942 across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Among those checked in the MMR, 722 drivers were found unable to speak Marathi and were subsequently issued notices. The Maharashtra State Transport Department had set August 15 as the deadline for drivers to learn Marathi after making knowledge of the language mandatory.Drivers go on strikeMumbai autorickshaw drivers began a three-day strike on Monday to oppose the government's rule, saying it could increase their financial burden, especially for those with limited formal education. Protesters also blocked traffic on Kandivali Link Road, raising concerns over the language requirement and penalties for non-compliance. Several drivers said older members of the community were finding it difficult to learn Marathi within the given deadline.What's next for Sonam Kapoor?Away from the controversy, Sonam Kapoor is yet to return to the big screen. She married Anand Ahuja in 2018 and welcomed their first son, Vayu, in August 2022, followed by their second son, Rudralokh, on March 29. The actress' last film was 'Blind' in 2023, and she was earlier expected to star in the screen adaptation of 'Battle For Bittora'.'Blind' was backed by Sujoy Ghosh and also featured Purab Kohli, Vinay Pathak and Lillete Dubey in supporting roles. articles.body: A major tribute is set to come up in Theni district for one of Tamil cinemaâs most respected filmmakers, Bharathiraja. The Tamil Nadu Government has announced plans to build a memorial hall in his birthplace, complete with a bronze statue. The announcement has now received appreciation from actor and Rajya Sabha MP Kamal Haasan, who praised the government for recognising the directorâs contribution to Tamil cinema. The proposed memorial is being seen as a fitting tribute to a filmmaker who brought the lives, emotions and landscapes of rural Tamil Nadu to the screen.Kamal Haasan hails TN governmentâs Bharathiraja memorial planKamal Haasan took to X to welcome the Tamil Nadu Governmentâs decision. He expressed his gratitude for honouring Bharathiraja in the land where the filmmaker was born. âMy heartfelt congratulations to the Tamil Nadu government for announcing that a memorial hall will be established in the very soil of his birth for director Bharathiraja, who captured the scent of the earth on screen. This is a gratitude rendered in the fullness of time,â Kamal Haasan said in his post. His statement highlighted the deep influence Bharathiraja had on Tamil cinema and the importance of remembering artists who changed the way stories were told on screen.Bharathiraja memorial hall to come up in Theni at Rs 2.5 croreThe memorial was announced in the Tamil Nadu Assembly by Minister Rajmohan during the demands for grants for the School Education, Tamil Development, and Information and Publicity departments. articles.title: Kate Hudson to produce How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel, 23 years on
articles.summary: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.
articles.body:
A sequel to How to Lose a Guy In 10 Days is in development, more than 20 years after the original hit rom-com was released, with original star Kate Hudson set to produce.

Work on the film is in the "very early days", with sources telling US media , external that both Hudson, 47, and Matthew McConaughey, 56, could reprise their roles from the first film.

In the original, Hudson played a magazine journalist called Andie who researches an article about modern dating. She convinces her boss she can get a man, Benjamin (McConaughey), to leave her in 10 days. Meanwhile, Benjamin bets his boss he can make any woman fall for him, with Andie his target.

Hudson will produce the sequel alongside Stacey Sher, who is behind hits such as Pulp Fiction and Matilda.

The movie grossed nearly $180m worldwide at the box office at the time.

The yellow silk Carolina Herrera dress Hudson wore near the end of the film also became a much talked-about piece of modern cinema fashion.

The star's most recent film role was in 2025's Song Sung Blue, which earned her a second Oscar nomination, following her first nod for Almost Famous back in 2001.

McConaughey's films include Dallas Buyer's Club, which won him an Oscar in 2014, The Wedding Planner and Magic Mike. He also appeared in 2008 movie Fool's Gold alongside Hudson.

Representatives for Hudson and McConaughey have been contacted for comment.

The new film would be the latest in a trend for nostalgic sequels in Hollywood, following The Devil Wears Prada 2 - which came 20 years after the original and also featured a magazine employee called Andy (played by Anne Hathaway).

In 2024, McConaughey told People magazine about his first meeting with Hudson before filming How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days.

"Immediately, we were comfortable with each other, and we jacked with each other, and we busted each other's chops, and we laughed a lot," he recalled.

"There was a bit of rock and roll exchange, like, 'Oh, this could be some heavyweight fun.' And I think that's why I was cast, and that's why, for whatever extent, it worked."

articles.body: Abhay Verma has opened up about his equation with contemporaries Ahaan Panday, Aneet Padda and Vedang Raina, making it clear that competition has no place among the young crop of actors in the industry. He heaped praise on his peers, especially Aneet Padda, with whom he shares a long-standing friendship.Abhay Verma praises Ahaan Panday and Vedang RainaTalking about Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda's success with 'Saiyaara' and Vedang Raina's acclaim for 'Main Vaapas Aaunga', Abhay Verma told News18 Showsha, "I've met Ahaan a couple of times. He's a lovely guy. I really respect him. Kudos to him and Aneet for breaking records with Saiyaara! I hope they do it with many more films. I wish the same for Vedang."Abhay Verma talks about his six-year bond with Aneet PaddaAbhay Verma shared that his friendship with Aneet Padda goes back several years, having first met her on the sets of a commercial. He said, "Aneet and I go back a long way, roughly six years. We did a Cadbury commercial, and we hit it off. She's from Amritsar, and I'm from Panipat, which are [culturally] very similar. She has a great sense of humour, and that's where we bonded. I'm so proud of her. She's a beautiful actor. There's no way she didn't deserve the love that came her way. She deserves all of it and more," he said.Speaking about the camaraderie among young actors today, Abhay said, "I believe that we, young actors, don't really have that sense of competition among us. We respect each other's dreams. We know the kind of stakes that are on us and the value of opportunities. That's why we respect the opportunities each of us gets."He added, "We're all here to serve a bigger purpose, which is to entertain the audience. What we've among us is beautiful. I speak to all them. I was recently speaking to Pratibha [Ranta], Rohit [Saraf] and Bhuvan [Bam] about The Revolutionaries."More about Abhay VermaOn the work front, he will next feature in Siddharth Anand's 'King' starring Shah Rukh Khan. The movie also features Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Arshad Warsi, Suhana Khan, Arshad Warsi, Saurabh Shukla, and more. articles.title: 'How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days' is coming back. Here's where 7 other 2000s rom-com revivals stand.
articles.summary: Paramount is developing a follow-up to the beloved rom-com, with hopes that Kate Hudson and Matthew McConaughey will reprise their roles.
articles.body:
After a real chick flick drought in recent years, fans of the genre are being treated to a whole slate of 2000s romantic-comedy sequels. The latest? The iconic How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days . Paramount Pictures is in early development on a follow-up to the 2003 movie, a source close to the project has confirmed to Deadline .

Hudson is producing alongside Stacey Sher, while Paramount and the filmmakers hope that Hudson and Matthew McConaughey will reprise their roles. However, no cast members are attached, and the project is still seeking a screenwriter, according to reports.

In the original movie, magazine writer Andie Anderson (Hudson) dates advertising executive Ben Barry (McConaughey) for an article about how to drive a man away in 10 days, unaware that he has bet he can make her fall in love with him in the same period. As is the rom-com way, they're bound for love, and their competing schemes become complicated when real feelings develop.

The film was a big hit, grossing over $178 million globally against a reported $50 million budget. Critics were less enthusiastic, with the film currently holding a 42% rating on Rotten Tomatoes , but audiences responded far more favorably. McConaughey said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast that it's the film that provides him with the most residual income.

"I think it's probably my favorite rom-com I've done, and a lot of people love that rom-com," McConaughey told host Josh Horowitz earlier this month . "And it still pays the best mailbox money of any film I've ever done. By far. By lengths."

No release date has been announced for the How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel — and it remains to be seen whether Andie and Ben invested in a second "love fern" and managed to keep it alive — but several other 2000s rom-com revivals are also being developed or discussed.

A third installment (after 2004's The Princess Diaries: Royal Engagement ) is in development, with Anne Hathaway returning as teen-turned-princess Mia Thermopolis. Whether Chris Pine, Héctor Elizondo and Heather Matarazzo reprise their roles remains to be seen, but we know for certain that Julie Andrews won't be back .

A follow-up to the soccer film that gave Keira Knightley her breakthrough role is also in development, with the original film's cowriter and director, Gurinder Chadha, working on a sequel . It's unknown whether Knightley or her colead, Parminder Nagra (who played Jesminder "Jess" Bhamra), will return — it all hinges on the strength of the script, Chadha told Deadline last year.

A tale of adolescence, adulthood and what's really important in life, this Jennifer Garner classic had viewers joining in the "Thriller" dance and wanting Mark Ruffalo as their boyfriend (that hasn't changed). Earlier this summer, Netflix announced a reimagining of the movie is coming , with People We Meet on Vacation 's Emily Bader and The Perks of Being a Wallflower's Logan Lerman leading a new cast. Garner is on board as an executive producer, and while she and original costar Judy Greer have also been photographed filming scenes for the project, the exact nature of their roles hasn't been confirmed.

A festive favorite, The Holiday 's star-studded ensemble included Cameron Diaz, Kate Winslet, Jude Law and Jack Black. Last year, it was announced that Apple TV+ has a limited series adaptation in the works, but none of the original cast or Nancy Meyers, who wrote and directed the original, are said to be involved. Instead, the revival will use the same plot: An American woman and a British woman swap homes and lives for the holidays, ultimately finding love.

This high school revenge comedy starred some of the biggest names of the moment: Jesse Metcalfe, Sophia Bush, Ashanti, Arielle Kebbel, Penn Badgley and Brittany Snow. A sequel was first talked about in 2024 , when Kebbel said "there is a script" that "does involve all the OG cast," but in February, Kebbel revealed during a podcast interview that the project, which she was developing and producing, is "on pause for now."

During a hiatus from Grey's Anatomy , Katherine Heigl filmed her lead role in 27 Dresses as Jane, who was a bridesmaid in 27 weddings while quietly longing for love herself. In May 2025, Heigl said she was "in talks" about a sequel but added that it would "have to be done right." Her love interest in the movie, James Marsden, confirmed he's open to reprising his role too. "That movie weirdly has legs that I'm not sure I anticipated it having," Marsden told E! News in 2023. "Just a fanbase that people — when they talk about romantic comedies — you don't really see too many of those made nowadays."

articles.title: Jennifer Love Hewitt can't stop dancing to Jamie Miller's viral hit 'Babydoll.' She's not alone.
articles.summary: The Welsh singer's catchy new song has attracted some famous fans — and they're helping him turn a TikTok dance into a viral moment.
articles.body:
There are only so many times a singer can post himself dancing to the same song before people start scrolling past. Jamie Miller seems to have found a way to fix that: by bringing in celebrity dance partners.

The Welsh singer has been promoting his infectious new song, "Babydoll," on TikTok and Instagram by two-stepping to the track in video after video. Lately, though, the people dancing alongside him have gotten a lot more recognizable. Jennifer Love Hewitt was the first famous face to join him. Dancing With the Stars ' Julianne Hough then followed, as did Antonio Cipriano , one of the breakout stars of Prime Video's series Off Campus .

Love Hewitt, in particular, really got into "Babydoll," using it in several TikToks and posting a video of herself playing it on the piano. "Playing around with it makes me smile," she wrote in the Aug. 12 post, thanking Miller for the song. Just days later, she was dancing alongside him , with Miller dubbing her "the most iconic babydoll there is."

The upbeat track was released Aug. 7, although Miller had been teasing it by posting snippets since late July. Now, each new "Babydoll" video comes with a question: Who will Miller get to join him next? Viral dances can come and go quickly, but rotating cameos give the same song a reason to keep popping up on people's feeds: it's the ideal formula for keeping a viral moment going.

Singer Role Model pulled off something similar with his track "Sally, When the Wine Runs Out," bringing a different "Sally" onstage during performances. Celebrities including Natalie Portman, Olivia Rodrigo and Charli xcx all took a turn, and clips of the cameos routinely went viral. Finding out who Sally would be became part of the attraction.

Sabrina Carpenter put her spin on the celebrity reveal during her Short n' Sweet tour, jokingly "arresting" famous faces for "being too hot" before singing "Juno." Millie Bobby Brown, Gigi Hadid and Salma Hayek were among those who got cuffed.

For anyone just discovering Miller through "Babydoll," he's been around for a while. The 28-year-old appeared on The Voice U.K. in 2017, where he competed on Jennifer Hudson's team and finished third. He released his debut album, titled Long Way Home , in 2024, but it did not chart on the Billboard 200.

Earlier this year, he signed with Republic Records , which is home to many of pop's biggest names, including Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande and the Weeknd. He has a sizable social media fanbase, including 4.1 million followers on TikTok and 1.2 million on Instagram — but "Babydoll" has put a new level of attention on the singer.

Love Hewitt has been posting about "Babydoll" enough that people have started wondering if she's on the record company's payroll. "People have asked me, 'Why are you putting it in all of your videos, besides the fact that it's addicting? Why are you pushing this song so much? Do you work for his record company?'" she said in a TikTok posted Aug. 23.

Love Hewitt clarified that she didn't work for his record company and said she first heard "Babydoll" on a day that "was not great." "Music finds you when you really need it," she said, and the song changed her mood: "The day was instantly better, more manageable, full of light."

Then she got to know Miller. "He is light. He is magic," the actor said. The first time they met in person was when they filmed their video together. Love Hewitt is clearly rooting for him now. "He is such a pure, kind, good human, who has worked so hard for this moment," she said. "We are all collectively gathering around him, rooting for him, becoming his magical, positive light army in the world."

How long the "Babydoll" moment lasts is anyone's guess. But for now, Miller has something plenty of singers would envy: a growing audience waiting to see what happens next.

articles.title: Kuku Kohli, Aruna Irani's husband and 'Phool Aur Kaante' director, passes away at 77 after suffering cardiac arrest
articles.summary: Veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli, best known for launching Ajay Devgnâs career with Phool Aur Kaante, has passed away at the age of 77. He suffered a card.
articles.body: Veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli, best known for launching Ajay Devgnâs career with Phool Aur Kaante, has passed away at the age of 77. He suffered a cardiac arrest on Tuesday evening. His wife, actress Aruna Iraniâs spokesperson, has confirmed the news to ETimes.Since Aruna Irani was not in a state of mind to speak, her spokesperson shared details about what had happened.According to the spokesperson, Kuku Kohli felt restless on Monday night and suffered a mild heart attack. He was admitted to Kokilaben Hospital that same night, where he underwent an angioplasty. Everything appeared to be normal after the procedure. However, on Tuesday at around 5:15 pm, he suffered a massive cardiac arrest.Meanwhile, Aruna was on a call with him and exchanging messages, and the two were reportedly in a playful mood. He even told her, âLetâs not go overboard.â Shortly afterwards, however, he began showing signs that something was wrong. After some time, he stopped responding.The final rites of veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli will take place on Wednesday, August 26, at Oshiwara Crematorium in Andheri West. His funeral procession will leave his residence at Green Acres, Lokhandwala Complex, Andheri West, at 10 am.Who was Kuku Kohli?Born Avtar Kohli on June 4, 1949, in Peshawar, Kuku Kohli was a director, writer, editor and screenwriter who spent more than three decades in the Indian film industry. Early in his career, he worked closely with legendary filmmaker Raj Kapoor, assisting him on films including Bobby, Prem Rog and Satyam Shivam Sundaram, where he honed his craft.He later served as second-unit director on Betaab, the film that launched Sunny Deol and Amrita Singh, and subsequently worked on Arjun, starring Sunny Deol and Dimple Kapadia.His biggest breakthrough came with Phool Aur Kaante in 1991, which marked Ajay Devgnâs debut as a leading actor and went on to achieve diamond jubilee status at the box office.A career spanning several hitsFollowing the success of Phool Aur Kaante, Kohli went on to direct several notable films, including Kohraam, starring Dharmendra, and Suhaag, featuring Ajay Devgn, Akshay Kumar and Karisma Kapoor.He also directed Haqeeqat, starring Ajay Devgn, Tabu and Amrish Puri. The film received seven nominations, including a Best Director nomination.His other works included Zulmi, starring Akshay Kumar and Twinkle Khanna, and Anari No. 1, which he co-produced with his wife.Kuku Kohliâs personal lifeKuku Kohli married veteran actress Aruna Irani in 1990. The couple reportedly did not have children together. This was Kohliâs second marriage, and he had two daughters from his first marriage to Rita Kohli.His passing marks the end of an influential chapter in Bollywoodâs commercial cinema of the 1990s, an era he helped shape through his collaborations with several leading stars of the time.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Jordi Cruz, chef, desvela la receta del salmorejo perfecto con un toque secreto: "Pequeños detalles marcan toda la diferencia"
articles.standfirst: El experimentado cocinero enumera las claves para conseguir un óptimo resultado de este clásico del verano
articles.summary: El experimentado cocinero enumera las claves para conseguir un óptimo resultado de este clásico del verano
articles.body: El periodo estival empieza a llegar a su fin, pero aún queda tiempo para elaborar las últimas recetas de los clásicos de este tiempo. El rey, por encima de todos, es el salmorejo. Jordi Cruz, chef y jurado de ‘MasterChef’, ha compartido en sus redes sociales los pasos que hay que seguir para conseguir el salmorejo perfecto con una receta “sencilla” y con “pocos ingredientes”. Lo primero que deja claro es que su salmorejo no lleva pimiento y tampoco vinagre, aunque matiza que esto es “un toque personal”. Para empezar con un buen pie en la elaboración, debemos procurar que “todos los ingredientes estén muy fríos antes de empezar”. Incluso, recomienda que puedes dejar el tomate cortado unos 20 minutos en el congelador. Después, hay que preparar la base del plato: “Tritura el tomate, el pimiento rojo (si decides utilizarlo) y el ajo sin germen hasta obtener una mezcla completamente fina”. Aunque hay personas que prefieren no añadir pan, Cruz sí lo incluye en su receta. Además, puntualiza que sea del “día anterior”. También se debe añadir en este momento la sal. “Con la trituradora en marcha, añade el aceite de oliva virgen extra poco a poco, en forma de hilo, hasta obtener una crema muy fina y sedosa”, apunta. También es gusto personal pasarlo por un colador, para eliminar posibles pieles o semillas y conseguir una textura todavía más elegante, antes de servirlo en la mesa. Por último, Jordi Cruz comparte un pequeño detalle para que la receta sea aún más perfecta y equilibrada: “Si utilizas pimiento rojo, aprovecha únicamente la carne y evita las semillas y las partes blancas del interior. Aporta un ligero dulzor y un extra de sabor sin alterar la receta”.

articles.summary: Jennifer Garner reveals she "panicked" about finances after her split from Ben Affleck, realizing she needed to become a serious earner for her kids.
articles.body: Jennifer Garner once "panicked" about her financial stability shortly after her marriage to Ben Affleck came to an end. During an episode of the "Aspire with Emma Grede" podcast, Garner — who shares three children with Affleck — opened up about her past fear that she would no longer be able to financially support herself and her children post-divorce and explained how she pushed through.  "I panicked when I was first out of my marriage and realized I had taken such a step back in my work," said Garner. "Suddenly I realized I don't know how long I'll be able to work. This isn't a career that's like, 'Hey, you're 60, you're 55, you're 43, come on, let's pay you more than you've ever made.' You know what I mean? That's not been traditionally the role. I was suddenly like, 'Wait a minute, I have to take care of myself, I have to take care of these kids. So what is it going to be?'" She had to be in Los Angeles for her children. "I can't leave these kids for six months at a time," she said. "I would love to. I love going on location, but it's not this time in my career." ‘THE OFFICE’ STAR JENNA FISCHER EXPOSES THE GRUELING REALITY THAT FORCED HER OFF TV Affleck and Garner met on the set of 2001's "Pearl Harbor," but didn't spark a romantic relationship until 2004, after starring alongside one another in the 2003 film "Daredevil." articles.title: Dolly Parton obituary: The country legend who sang from the heart
articles.summary: The singer, songwriter and actress is known for timeless hits including Jolene and I Will Always Love You.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, the country singer from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, will be remembered for her songs that told beautiful stories so honestly, such as Coat of Many Colors, Jolene and I Will Always Love You.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote in excess of 3,000 songs.

Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy.â

She was also a savvy businesswoman who wasn't afraid to make tough decisions. Armed with a quick wit and southern charm, she took control of her showbusiness career that spanned more than 60 years.

Dolly Rebecca Parton was born in 1946, the fourth of 12 children, into a poor farming family who lived in a one-bedroom cabin in Tennessee.

Her father, Robert Lee Parton, was a tobacco farmer and paid a missionary a sack of cornmeal for delivering her.

There was already music in the family - her mother, Avie Lee, sang folk songs all the time and her aunt played the guitar and wrote songs.

During some of Parton's earliest performances, her uncle, Bill Owens, accompanied her on the guitar - formative years for the future music legend.

From the age of six, she sang in the local church where her grandfather was the pastor, and was performing on her local TV station by the time she was a teenager.

In 1959, when she was 13 years old, Parton performed with Uncle Bill at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville - a live broadcast that is regarded as country music's biggest stage.

She was introduced by Johnny Cash and received three encores.

During her teenage years, Parton began to model herself on a local character who was known as the âtown trampâ.

The lady wore bright red nail polish, low-cut tops and high heels - young Dolly thought she was beautiful.

When people said to her: âShe ainât nothing but trashâ, Parton would reply: "Well, thatâs what Iâm gonna be when I grow upâ.

Parton sang â Iâm just a backwards Barbie / too much make-up, too much hair â, but her image was both a coat of armour and an astute disguise that helped get her noticed in showbusiness.

She would get ahead of the jokes by making them first, and had a quick and simple response for anyone who suggested she should tone it down: "Go to hell."

After graduating from high school in 1964, she moved to Nashville to launch her singing career and met her future husband, Carl Dean, on her very first day.

They married two years later and remained together until his death in 2025.

In Nashville, Parton's singing caught the eye of country performer Porter Wagoner, who hired her to perform on his television programme.

Over the next seven years, the pair became one of country music's most popular duos, releasing so many duets that many fans assumed they were a couple.

But their relationship was a complicated one, and as Parton's solo career started to rise, so did tensions behind the scenes.

Writing in her book Star of the Show: My Life on Stage, Parton said Wagoner saw her success away from his show as a "threat".

While travelling with Wagoner on a tour bus in 1969, Parton wrote Coat of Many Colors, a beautifully emotive tale of how she grew up poor, but rich with love.

Scrawled on the back of one of Wagoner's dry cleaning receipts, it was rated by Rolling Stone magazine , external as her second best-ever song. Years later, Parton named her own children's book Coat of Many Colors, and it was the name of a 2015 TV movie based on her life.

"It's a song that's just stood by me... it's created a life of many colours for me," she said.

Despite being unable to read sheet music, Parton played several instruments including the banjo, harp, piano and saxophone.

She had her first number one hit - and first Grammy nomination - with the song Joshua in 1971 and finally left The Porter Wagoner Show in 1974 to concentrate on her solo career.

To say goodbye to him, she wrote I Will Always Love You , a song that many think is about two lovers parting ways.

"That's the prettiest song I ever heard," Wagoner cried when he first heard it, her website says.

The same year, Elvis Presley was set to record a cover of the song, but Parton pulled the deal when his manager demanded half of the songwriting rights.

She cried all night at the difficult decision, and Priscilla Presley later told her that Elvis sang the song to her during their divorce.

In 1992, Whitney Houston transformed it into a now-iconic power ballad.

Parton said she was driving when she first heard the cover and had to pull over: âWhen I heard her go from the a cappella into the music part, I honestly thought I was going to have a heart attack, it was one of the most overwhelming things.â

Houston's cover of Parton's âsad little country songâ was one of the proudest moments of her life, she said.

Parton re-recorded the song for The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas, a 1982 film in which she starred and was nominated for a Golden Globe for best actress.

Another of her most famous songs was released in 1974 - Jolene.

Showing her aching vulnerability, it's about a bank clerk with flaming locks of auburn hair who flirted with her husband.

" Jolene, I'm begging of you, please don't take my man ," she pleads.

Parton said her husband, who was notoriously private, was a bit embarrassed by the song. But it was nothing serious - just a running joke between them: "I was saying, 'Hell, you're spending a lot of time at the bank. I don't believe we've got that kind of money.'"

The song has been covered by many artists including The White Stripes, Miley Cyrus and BeyoncÃ©, who changed up the lyrics to the more ominous: " I'm warning you, don't come for my man. "

In the years to come, Dolly Parton's success only grew, with more hits, nominations and awards - she won her first Grammy in 1978 for Here You Come Again.

It was the theme song that Dolly Parton wrote for the 1980 movie 9 to 5 that fully propelled her to stardom.

Actress Jane Fonda, who produced and starred in the film about women being discriminated against in the workplace, made a deal with Parton - she'd star in the film if she could also write the theme song.

Realising her nails clicking together sounded like a typewriter, she wrote 9 to 5 while waiting around on set. Fonda said she realised straight away that it wasn't just a theme song - it was an anthem.

The film was a big success at the box office and the song won several awards, including a Golden Globe.

'I look like a woman but I think like a man'

Parton was a successful and shrewd businesswoman, and in 2022 was listed by Forbes as one of America's richest self-made women , external .

"I look like a woman but I think like a man. I've done business with men who think I'm as silly as I look. By the time they realise I'm not, I've got the money and gone," she once said.

Her physical appearance - the costumes, wigs, long painted nails and high heels - were merely a facade of a stereotypical âdumb blondeâ. But she always said she knew she wasn't dumb "and I also know that I'm not blonde".

She had her own record label, Dolly Records, and co-owned The Dollywood Company, which manages entertainment venues, a theme park, a water park and a resort.

In 1986, she opened her Dollywood amusement park in the foothills of her beloved Smoky Mountains. As well as rollercoasters, it is home to the largest sanctuary for non-releasable bald eagles in the world. Its rehabilitation and breeding work has won awards and in 2007, the bald eagle was removed from the endangered species list.

Despite her wealth and success, Parton remained humble and supported the communities where she grew up.

Inspired by her father who couldnât read or write, she launched the Imagination Library in 1999, which gave free books to children in Tennessee. It has since expanded to Australia, the UK, Ireland and Canada, sending out millions of free books every year.

Her non-profit organisation, The Dollywood Foundation, has funded scholarships, hospitals and donated to flood and wildfire victims.

In 2020, as the Covid-19 pandemic gripped the world, Parton donated $1m (Â£716,000) to the Vanderbilt University Medical Centre which helped to fund the Moderna vaccine.

How Dolly Parton became the worldâs best-loved celebrity

In later years, Parton had to postpone or cancel several shows for health treatment.

In May 2026, she postponed an upcoming Las Vegas residency because of treatment for kidney stones, saying it would take some time to heal and be "stage-performance ready".

"I can't be dizzy carrying around banjos, guitars and such on five-inch heels - and you know that I'm going to be wearing them," she said in a video message.

"Not to mention all those heavy rhinestone outfits, the big hair, my big... uh, personality," she joked.

Parton spoke graciously throughout her career with humour and intelligence. She steered clear of politics, saying she didn't want to alienate half her audience.

She was a courageous and talented trailblazer for country music at a time when women were not taken seriously in the industry, especially as solo artists.

Parton said she hoped to be remembered for her songwriting and as somebody who took her work seriously, but not herself.

She once offered this advice: âNever ignore your roots, your home, or your hair."

It's guidance that she stayed true to throughout her life.

articles.title: Javier Bardem: "España es donde quiero estar, donde vivo, donde cotizo, donde quiero que mis hijos crezcan"
articles.standfirst: El actor se sincera en una entrevista para promocionar 'El ser querido'
articles.summary: El actor se sincera en una entrevista para promocionar 'El ser querido'
articles.body: Javier Bardem ha reivindicado su amor por el cine de España y por el propio país. "El cine español es mi cine, es el cine donde yo he crecido. Luego he tenido la oportunidad de trabajar fuera y eso es un lujo, pero, lo dije el otro día, yo nunca he vivido fuera, he vivido siempre en España", ha explicado en una entrevista a EFE. El actor ha insistido en que no tiene ninguna intención de alejarse de su país natal: "Es aquí donde yo quiero estar, donde quiero que mis hijos crezcan, donde vivo, donde cotizo, donde me preocupa más lo que pasa a todos los niveles. Es donde está mi familia, donde están mis hermanos, donde están mis amigos. Es todo". El actor, ganador de un Oscar al mejor actor de reparto por 'No Country for Old Men', en 2007, vive un gran momento profesional a sus 57 años. Javier Bardem es el protagonista de 'El ser querido', película dirigida por Rodrigo Sorogoyen que se estrena este miércoles en las salas de cine, después de presentarse en el festival de Cannes. El actor interpreta a Esteban Martínez, un director de cine, con un marcado carácter violento, y también un padre ausente. "Ese es el problema generacional que ha sufrido, que no fue educado para ser consciente del dolor que puede provocar", ha detallado Bardem en la entrevista. El artista ha definido la trama de 'El ser querido' como una historia de abandono. "Todos hemos sentido el abandono en algún momento de nuestra vida, incluso a veces por nosotros mismos. Para sentirse involucrado con la historia no hace falta haber sido abandonado por tu padre", ha argumentado Javier Bardem. La película de Rodrigo Sorogoyen se podrá ver también en los cines de Estados Unidos y Canadá, motivo de gran satisfacción para el director, como ha expresado en un comunicado.

articles.title: Muere Dolly Parton, legendaria cantante de country, a los 80 años
articles.standfirst: La causa de su fallecimiento no ha sido revelada, por el momento
articles.summary: La causa de su fallecimiento no ha sido revelada, por el momento
articles.body: Luto en el mundo de la música después de conocerse el fallecimiento de Dolly Parton a los 80 años. La causa de la muerte no ha sido revelada, pero su familia ya la ha despedido en su perfil oficial de Instagram a través de un vídeo en el que explica lo sucedido su sobrino, Bryan Seaver, en nombre de toda la familia. Brilló en la música country con más de 25 canciones que fueron número 1 en los Estados Unidos, muchas de ellas también en el mundo. "Falleció en paz hoy en Nashville", reza la descripción del post publicado. Su canción más conocida es ‘I Will Always Love You’, una balada que compuso tras romper su relación con Wagoner en 1974. Además, en 1992 interpretó junto a Whitney Houston la banda sonora de la famosa película ‘El guardaespaldas’. Otra canción por la que es muy reconocida es ‘Jolene’, de 1973, de la que un cantante como Miley Cyrus ha hecho covers. En el vídeo, su sobrino, Seaver, explica: “Una vida brillante como un diamante que resplandeció para que el mundo la viera, Dolly siempre será una inspiración no solo por su música atemporal y su prolífica obra como compositora, sino también por su ingenio, calidez y bondad que nos hicieron sentir a todos como en familia”. Continúa diciendo: “El legado de Dolly Parton es de amor, compasión y resiliencia. Con una carrera de siete décadas, inspiró a varias generaciones de artistas y fans con su música y un compromiso inquebrantable para hacer del mundo un lugar mejor. Sus canciones seguirán resonando en personas de todas las edades, y su labor filantrópica tendrá un impacto duradero”. La propia artista habló abiertamente de sus problemas de salud, lo hizo a través de un post en redes sociales. Todo comenzó el 28 de septiembre de 2025, cancelando seis conciertos en diciembre en el Caesars Palace de Las Vegas, en lo que era su regreso a los escenarios. Además, el 30 de septiembre no pudo asistir a la ceremonia de entrega de los Premios de los Gobernadores de la Academia de Artes y Ciencias Cinematográficas, donde iba a recibir el Premio Humanitario Jean Hersholt. “Como muchos de ustedes saben, he estado lidiando con algunos problemas de salud y mis médicos me dicen que debo someterme a algunos procedimientos. Como bromeé con ellos, debe ser hora de mi revisión de los 100.000 kilómetros, ¡aunque no es el típico viaje a mi cirujano plástico!”, dijo en su momento, bromeando. “Si bien podré seguir trabajando en todos mis proyectos desde aquí en Nashville, solo necesito un poco de tiempo para prepararme para el espectáculo, como dicen. Y no se preocupen por que deje el negocio porque Dios aún no ha dicho nada sobre parar. Pero creo que Él me está diciendo que baje el ritmo ahora para poder estar lista para más grandes aventuras con todos ustedes. Los quiero y gracias por su comprensión”. Sin embargo, el 5 de mayo de 2026, publicó otro post en el que mencionaba directamente qué es lo que le pasaba: “Estoy aquí para darles una actualización sobre mi salud, y tengo buenas noticias y un poquito de malas. Estoy respondiendo muy bien a la medicación y a los tratamientos y sigo mejorando cada día”. “Ya saben que les he contado antes que siempre he tenido problemas con los cálculos renales. Mi sistema inmunológico y digestivo se desajustaron completamente en los últimos dos años y que están trabajando para reconstruirlos y fortalecerlos y volver a estar en forma pront”, sentenció hace tres meses.

articles.title: Dolly Parton: A life in pictures
articles.summary: The singer rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most beloved entertainers in the world.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, the country music superstar from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most beloved entertainers in the world.

Over a career spanning more than 60 years, she sold more than 100 million records, wrote more than 3,000 songs and won 11 Grammy Awards, including a lifetime achievement honour.

Yet she has always described herself first and foremost as a songwriter. "It's my way of expressing myself. It's my therapy," she once said.

Dolly Parton grew up in poverty in a one-room cabin on the banks of the Little Pigeon River in Tennessee's Smoky Mountains, the fourth of 12 children.

She performed on local radio and television as a child and recorded her first single at 13.

After moving to Nashville the day after graduating from Sevier County High School, Dolly Parton scored her first solo hit with Dumb Blonde in 1966.

In 1967, country star Porter Wagoner invited Parton to join The Porter Wagoner Show, giving her a regular role on his nationally syndicated television programme as well as a place in his touring stage show.

Her breakthrough came with the album Hello, I'm Dolly.

Dolly Parton became a member of the Grand Ole Opry on January 4, 1969.

She has described the Opry as the "church of my heart" and said performing there was a lifelong dream.

In one remarkable 1973 writing session, Parton penned two of her signature hits â Jolene and I Will Always Love You.

Having written thousands of songs across her decades-long career, Parton said songwriting was her greatest form of self-expression.

Known for her larger-than-life image, Dolly Parton combined rhinestones, wit and charm to sustain a career that crossed from country to mainstream pop.

She headlined festivals and became a global star with albums such as Here You Come Again.

Parton also became known for memorable collaborations, notably with Kenny Rogers, whose duet Islands in the Stream became one of the defining hits of the 1980s.

While Dolly Parton is best known for her decades-spanning music career, her work as an actor has also left a lasting impression on film audiences.

Parton's breakout screen role came in the 1980 workplace comedy 9 to 5, where she starred alongside Jane Fonda, Lily Tomlin and Dabney Coleman.

Her portrayal of Doralee Rhodes combined comic timing with warmth, helping to redefine expectations of performers crossing over from music into film.

She followed this with roles in films such as The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas, alongside Burt Reynolds, and Steel Magnolias.

The latter featured an ensemble cast including Julia Roberts and Sally Field alongside Sylvester Stallone.

In these performances, Parton demonstrated a balance of humour and emotional depth, often anchoring scenes with a distinctly understated presence.

In 1986 Dolly Parton opened Dollywood, a theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, near her birthplace.

It became a major tourist attraction - one of the most visited regional theme parks in the USA.

The park's success helped fund Parton's charitable foundation and literacy programme.

Through her Imagination Library, founded in honour of her father who could not read, Dolly Parton has given away more than 100 million free books to children around the world.

Her own book, Coat of Many Colours, was the 100 millionth book that programme donated to the US Library of Congress collection.

A council in Scotland announced it would dedicate a day to Dolly Parton every year to mark the impact of her reading scheme.

Parton personally donated millions to medical research and disaster relief.

The singer also led several major disaster-relief efforts, most notably creating the My People Fund after the 2016 Great Smoky Mountains wildfires which distributed about $10m to families who lost homes.

She lined up an all-star list of performers for a three-hour telethon to raise money.

In 2024, she pledged $2m for Hurricane Helene relief in East Tennessee and Appalachia, combining a personal donation with matching support from her businesses and foundation.

Parton's 2014 Glastonbury Festival appearance quickly became one of the defining "Legends" slot performances in the event's history.

Drawing one of the festival's biggest-ever daytime crowds - estimated at more than 180,000 - she turned the Pyramid Stage into a mass singalong, with renditions of Jolene, 9 to 5 and I Will Always Love You prompting scenes of near-universal audience participation.

In 2019, Parton celebrated 50 years as an Opry member with a major televised special called Dolly Parton: 50 Years at the Opry.

The event featured performances and tributes from other country artists.

Her decades-spanning relationship with the Opry helped cement its status as both a guardian of country music tradition and a stage for modern stars.

Parton gradually began to step away from major touring, saying she no longer wanted to spend long stretches on the road.

Instead, she focused on selective live shows, new recording projects and screen appearances including Dolly Parton's Heartstrings, Mountain Magic and Christmas on the Square for Netflix.

In 2021, Parton publicly received a Covid-19 vaccine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, using the moment to encourage others to do the same.

She sang an adapted version of her hit Jolene, singing: "Vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, I'm begging of you, please don't hesitate."

Parton's 2022 induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame marked a characteristically self-aware turn.

Having initially said she had not "earned" the honour, she later embraced it with humour - declaring "I'm a rock star now" - before performing her new song Rockin', written especially for the ceremony, a symbolic step toward her later rock album Rockstar.

In 2023, Parton delivered another headline-grabbing live moment when she performed at the Dallas Cowboys' Thanksgiving halftime show, appearing in a rhinestone-studded Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders outfit.

More recently, Parton continued to balance personal loss with new creative work.

Following the death of her husband Carl Dean in 2025, she released If You Hadn't Been There in tribute, while also continuing development of Dolly: A True Original Musical, the stage production based on her life and career.

In early 2026, Parton gave a pre-recorded tribute speech for Ozzy Osbourne at the BRIT Awards in Manchester, where Ozzy received a posthumous Lifetime Achievement Award.

Her speech was short but was one of the emotional highlights of the ceremony.

Parton had been due to return to the stage for a short Las Vegas residency, but announced this month that she was cancelling the run because of health issues, telling fans she needed "a little more time to heal".

She will remain a cultural icon remembered for her generosity and humour, as well as her extraordinary songwriting - the craft at the heart of a catalogue that has shaped modern country music and crossed generations.

articles.title: Dolly Parton de qué murió: La leyenda del country falleció a los 80 años
articles.summary: Fallece la legendaria cantante.
articles.body: La legendaria cantante y compositora de música country Dolly Parton se despidió de los años 80, según anunció su familia. Su muerte fue anunciada por su sobrino Brian Seaver en Instagram. "Me imaginaba la tristeza de este momento, pero no la había sentido de verdad hasta ahora", dijo. "Es un homenaje, un homenaje que combina un orgullo absoluto con una profunda tristeza". Dolly Parton nació el 19 de enero de 1946 en Pittman Center, Tennessee, y creció en una familia numerosa en una cabaña de una sola habitación. Era una de doce hermanos, y su crianza en la zona rural de Tennessee se convirtió en una importante fuente de inspiración para sus composiciones. Su talento musical se manifestó a una edad muy temprana. De niña, actuaba en la televisión local y se presentó en el Grand Ole Opry de Nashville con tan solo 13 años. Tras graduarse de la escuela secundaria en 1964, Parton se mudó a Nashville y comenzó a forjar su carrera como compositora e intérprete. Su colaboración con Porter Wagoner la consolidó como una gran estrella de la música country, pero Parton finalmente se independizó para seguir su propio camino. Esta transición dio lugar a algunas de las canciones que definirían su legado, como Jolene y I Will Always Love You. La influencia de Parton superó con creces los límites tradicionales de la música country. Su éxito de 1980, "9 to 5", fue un gran éxito pop y, además, dio título a la película que protagonizó junto a Jane Fonda y Lily Tomlin. Posteriormente, apareció en películas como "Magnolias de acero" y "La mejor casa de putas de Texas". También fue una de las compositoras más exitosas comercialmente de la música estadounidense. Reuters informó que Parton vendió más de 100 millones de discos en todo el mundo, y 25 de sus canciones alcanzaron el número 1 en la lista de éxitos country de Billboard. Ganó 11 premios Grammy, incluyendo un premio a la trayectoria, y fue incluida en el Salón de la Fama del Rock & Roll en 2022. "I Will Always Love You" se convirtió en una canción particularmente significativa para su legado. Parton la escribió originalmente como una despedida a Wagoner, pero la exitosa versión de Whitney Houston la dio a conocer a otra generación y la convirtió en uno de los sencillos más exitosos comercialmente jamás grabados por una artista femenina. Los logros de Parton también se extendieron al mundo empresarial. Transformó un parque temático de Tennessee en Dollywood, que se convirtió en un importante destino turístico y una fuerza económica significativa en la región. Quizás su contribución más perdurable fuera del mundo del espectáculo fue la Biblioteca de la Imaginación de la Fundación Dollywood. Esta iniciativa de alfabetización, establecida en 1995, proporcionaba libros gratuitos a niños pequeños y, con el tiempo, se expandió más allá de Tennessee a varios países. El programa ha distribuido más de 150 millones de libros, según The Guardian. Parton también donó un millón de dólares para la investigación de la vacuna contra la COVID-19 en la Universidad de Vanderbilt en 2020, convirtiéndose en una importante patrocinadora financiera de la investigación vinculada al desarrollo de la vacuna de Moderna. Sus últimos años estuvieron marcados por nuevos proyectos. Su sitio web oficial destacó recientemente las certificaciones de su nueva música y una producción de Broadway, DOLLY: A True Original Musical, cuyo estreno estaba previsto para diciembre de 2026. Hasta el momento, la familia no ha confirmado la causa de la muerte de Dolly Parton. Sin embargo, la cantante había enfrentado severon problemas de salud en los últimos meses. Parton anunció repentinamente en mayo de 2026 que cancelaba un espectáculo en Las Vegas y añadio había estado recibiendo tratamiento para cálculos renales durante varios años. La muerte de Parton cierra uno de los capítulos más notables del entretenimiento estadounidense moderno. Logró desenvolverse con éxito entre la música country, el pop, el cine, la televisión, los negocios y la filantropía, manteniendo siempre una conexión con sus raíces de Tennessee, que la moldearon. Para generaciones de fans, su voz inconfundible, sus composiciones y su generosidad serán inseparables de la historia de la música estadounidense.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere’s rep slams ‘gossip and speculation’ as death investigation deepens
articles.summary: The DEA is investigating Hayden Panettiere's death as her team says key details have yet to emerge and urges people with information to contact police.
articles.body: Hayden Panettiere’s team slammed the "gossip and speculation" that erupted after her shocking death and warned that the public still didn’t know the full story as investigators searched for answers. Her representative condemned the speculation surrounding Panettiere’s final hours and accused outsiders of turning her death into fodder for gossip. "Many people who were not close to Hayden are using her death as an opportunity to fuel gossip and speculation about a situation they knew very little about," Panettiere's rep said in a statement shared with US Weekly. "It is deeply disrespectful to her memory and to those who knew and loved her and are actively grieving this tremendous loss." HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S BOYFRIEND’S BROTHER REVEALS WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE AIRBNB BEFORE ACTRESS'S DEATH As the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) joined the investigation into Panettiere's death, her rep urged anyone with information to come forward. "If you have legitimate information that could be helpful, please contact law enforcement rather than turning to social media to speculate publicly about something you do not fully understand." POLICE SHOW UP AT HOME LINKED TO HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S ON-AND-OFF BOYFRIEND DAYS AFTER HER SUDDEN DEATH Panettiere's team also hinted that key details surrounding Panettiere’s death had yet to emerge. articles.title: There was only one Dolly Parton. See her remarkable life in photos.
articles.summary: Parton was the purest kind of pop icon, with an image and a sound that was universally beloved yet entirely her own.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton died in Nashville on Tuesday at the age of 80 , but her outsize legacy will live on. Over a peerless six-decade career as a country singer, songwriter, entertainer and entrepreneur, Parton transmuted her hardscrabble roots as the daughter of an illiterate Tennessee sharecropper into the purest kind of pop iconography: an image and a sound that was universally beloved yet entirely her own.

In 2019, the New York Times ran a story with the headline "Is There Anything We Can All Agree On?" The answer? "Yes: Dolly Parton."

Among the things that everyone agreed on was Parton's prodigious talent. A child performer on local radio and television programs, she first broke through, in 1966, with a single called "Dumb Blonde." "Just because I'm blonde, don't think I'm dumb," Parton sang in the chorus. "'Cause this dumb blonde ain't nobody's fool."

The song was written by someone else, but the sentiment would come to define Parton's layered public persona: a voluptuous, rhinestone-studded, bouffant-bewigged " Backwoods Barbie " who happened to be the shrewdest of businesswomen, the sharpest of lyricists and the most generous of philanthropists.

"I've created this and played it up — the makeup, the whole persona," Parton said in a 2002 interview . "But this isn't all I am. It's not even most of what I am. Hopefully people can see beneath the hair to know there's a brain, beneath the boobs to know there's a heart and behind all the other stuff to know there's some talent."

Parton penned most of her subsequent hits herself. She found early success duetting with fellow country singer Porter Wagoner, but struck out on her own in the mid-1970s after a string of solo singles — " Joshua ," " Coat of Many Colors ," " Touch Your Woman ," My Tennessee Mountain Home ," "Travelin' Man," "Jolene" — made the country Top 20.

In 1974, Parton wrote "I Will Always Love You" about her professional split from Wagoner; the song was a hit for Parton multiple times (1974, 1982, 1995), and eventually topped the charts for 14 weeks when Whitney Houston covered it for The Bodyguard soundtrack in 1992.

All told, Parton was the top-ranking female singer on country radio from 1967 to 1993, with a total of 25 No. 1 country singles. She published 3,000 songs in her lifetime, blazing a trail for other women along the way. "I can't imagine anybody, especially in country, who doesn't try to emulate Dolly in some way," singer-songwriter Emmylou Harris said in 2006.

The fact that Parton accomplished so much in music while also challenging cultural stereotypes, starring in movies, opening a theme park, funding education programs and emphasizing hope, resilience, empathy and acceptance, both on stage and off — it all made her easy to agree on. It's hard to imagine that anyone else could have pulled it off, or will ever come close again.

articles.title: STEVE DOOCY: The Dolly Parton I saw when the cameras stopped rolling
articles.summary: Steve Doocy reflects on interviewing Dolly Parton half a dozen times, revealing the professionalism and kindness she showed when cameras weren't rolling.
articles.body: On August 23, 2016, ten years ago this week, I was with Dolly Parton in New York City, and we were about to do a live segment on FOX & Friends. Just before we went on, I asked Dolly if I could take a selfie with her. She looked at me and said, "Why would you want a picture with little ol’ me?" DOLLY PARTON DEAD AT 80 AS COUNTRY MUSIC WORLD MOURNS BELOVED ICON WHOSE SONGS SHAPED GENERATIONS I laughed and said, "Hello…Dolly—you’re Dolly Parton!" That was Dolly. Over my years on "FOX & Friends," I was lucky enough to interview her probably half a dozen times. And here’s something people watching at home wouldn’t necessarily know: Dolly was always on time. Always prepared. Always a professional. In morning television, where guests sometimes arrive moments before they’re supposed to be on live TV—or occasionally after—that matters! Dolly showed up ready to go. And the minute the camera came on, so did that Dolly magic. She was funny, quick, kind and incredibly smart. She knew exactly what she wanted to say, but somehow never let an interview feel rehearsed. You could ask her a serious question and get a thoughtful answer, then a few seconds later she’d say something hilarious that nobody saw coming. DOLLY PARTON'S CALIFORNIA RETREAT WITH WIG ROOM AND DOLLYWOOD BIRDHOUSE LISTS FOR $1.95M She was simply great television. But what I remember most is that she was just as nice when the cameras weren’t rolling. For all her fame, Dolly always seemed to understand something important: being nice to people doesn’t cost a thing. Underneath the rhinestones, the big hair and that unmistakable Tennessee voice was a very savvy businesswoman. Dolly didn’t just build a career. She built an empire. She understood her audience, understood her brand and, most importantly, understood people. And somehow, through all that enormous success, she remained remarkably down-to-earth. A few years ago, I interviewed Dolly and my friend James Patterson about the novel they wrote together, "Run, Rose, Run". Later, when I toured James’ Florida home, he showed me one of his prized possessions: a guitar Dolly had given him, inscribed with a birthday message that ended, naturally, "I will always love you." That was Dolly, too. And there’s another connection I had completely forgotten until today. During the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge craze in 2014, Kenny Rogers was challenged by Lionel Richie. Kenny then nominated three people to go next: Garth Brooks, Dolly Parton…and me. To this day, I’m still not entirely sure how Steve Doocy wound up on a list with Garth Brooks and Dolly Parton—but I’m glad I did! Dolly was one of those rare people who seemed to be exactly the same person when the cameras were off as when they were on. Funny. Kind. Smart. Professional. And completely original. She wrote songs that generations know by heart. She became a legendary entertainer, songwriter and businesswoman. She gave away millions of books to children. And she never seemed to forget where she came from—or lose her wonderful ability to laugh at herself. For all her fame, Dolly always seemed to understand something important: being nice to people doesn’t cost a thing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I’m grateful our paths crossed so many times. And today, ten years later, I’m especially grateful I asked for that selfie. Godspeed, Dolly. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Thanks for the music, the laughs, the memories—and the kindness. There will never be another one quite like you. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM STEVE DOOCY

articles.title: From '9 to 5' to 'Steel Magnolias,' 5 Dolly Parton movies to revisit
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's legacy extended well beyond country music, with memorable film roles, original songs and performances that made her a Hollywood favorite.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton has died at age 80, her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, announced in an Instagram video on Tuesday. While most people associate the Queen of Country with hits like "Jolene," "Coat of Many Colors" and "Islands in the Stream" — and will no doubt be streaming her music in the wake of her death — the icon's legacy extends into the world of film as well.

The blond, bubbly, rhinestone-loving Tennessee native appeared in numerous movies and provided music for many of them. The 1980 film 9 to 5 , which marked her acting debut, included her hit song of the same name and earned her an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song. But it was just the beginning of a memorable, albeit modest — she has about a dozen feature film credits, in addition to a slew of made-for-TV movies — acting career.

Eager to revisit Parton's filmography? Here's a refresher on her onscreen performances.

The 1980 comedy, directed by Colin Higgins, stars Parton alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin as office workers who rebel against their sexist boss.

Parton wrote the song "9 to 5" while working on the film's set, after realizing that her long acrylic nails could mimic the sound of a typewriter . The track became one of the biggest hits of the decade and earned Parton her first Oscar nomination. (She would later be nominated again for Best Original Song for "Travelin' Thru," the theme song to the 2005 film Transamerica .)

The movie 9 to 5 later inspired a 1982 TV series that ran for five seasons, as well as a Broadway musical for which Parton wrote the music and lyrics. The film's feminist themes also created an enduring legacy, with a 2022 documentary, Still Working 9 to 5, exploring its impact on gender equity.

In a 2019 interview with the Los Angeles Times , Parton reflected on the film's message: "Just keep pushing, hoping for equal pay for equal work, getting the respect that we need. I'll always be about that."

How to watch: 9 to 5 is currently streaming on Philo and is available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas (1982)

Parton's second film was also a commercial success, reteaming her with 9 to 5 director Colin Higgins. In the film, Parton portrayed Miss Mona, who must fight to save her "Chicken Ranch" brothel after a public campaign to shut it down. The film earned Parton a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress. She also rerecorded her 1974 song "I Will Always Love You" for the film, which then dominated the country charts.

Parton was particularly excited to do the film due to her costar, Burt Reynolds. "They have to rewrite it a little for Burt and me, 'cause I said I wouldn't do it unless I got to kiss him," she joked in a 1980 interview with Roger Ebert , prior to filming.

But the shoot didn't meet her expectations. In her 1994 autobiography, she called the film's production "a miserable, spirit-numbing ordeal."

How to watch: The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas is currently available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

Can you imagine Sylvester Stallone as a country singer? In the musical comedy Rhinestone , which was co-written by Stallone, Parton's nightclub singer bets that she can turn New York City cabbie Nick (Stallone) into a crooner in order to get out of her dead-end contract.

While Stallone called Rhinestone "the most fun I ever had on a movie," the film was a flop, with the actor admitting that "silly comedy" didn't quite work for him. Still, the soundtrack, much of which was penned and performed by Parton, was a success , with the song "Tennessee Homesick Blues" reaching the top of the country charts and "God Won't Get You" peaking at number 10. Parton also scored a Grammy nod for "Tennessee Homesick Blues" in the Best Country Vocal Performance, Female category.

How to watch: Rhinestone is currently unavailable ondigital streaming. You can purchase a DVD copy on Amazon .

This ensemble film, about the lives of a group of Louisiana women based on the 1987 play of the same name, was a massive hit. It starred Parton as Truvy Jones, owner of a small-town beauty shop, alongside Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis, Daryl Hannah and Julia Roberts. The film earned Roberts her first Academy Award nomination.

"I thought this was the perfect role for me because if I had not made it in the business, I would have been a beautician because I would have had to have got discount prices on makeup and hair color and bleach, and all of that," Parton told Vanity Fair in 2020. "So I felt like Truvy. I felt like I was fit right in that spot, and I really liked the role that I played. And that was a huge success. I loved working with all those women."

Unlike Parton's other work, this one was not centered on music. Though Parton wrote the song "Eagle When She Flies" for the movie, the filmmakers ultimately chose not to use a theme song for the film . Instead, the track — hailed by Rolling Stone as one of the best of Parton's career — became the title song off her 1991 album.

How to watch: Steel Magnolias is currently available to stream free with ads on Pluto TV .

In this romantic comedy, Parton stars as a small-town woman who stumbles into a job giving advice on the radio in Chicago, and falls for the investigative journalist (James Woods) who begins looking into her background.

Ten of Parton's songs were used for the film's soundtrack, including a rerecording of her 1976 song "Light of a Clear Blue Morning."

In a 1992 press conference, Parton revealed that the script had come her way seven years before the film got made. Per Parton, the role was eventually given to her Steel Magnolias costar Roberts, who eventually passed, allowing Parton to pick it up.

"We certainly `Dollyized' it," Parton said at the time. "It was a wonderful script, but a lot of [the dialogue] was ad-libbed. I can't hardly not ad-lib when I get something like this."

She also spoke about how proud she was to do the film, which she felt embodied so much of who she was.

"If I died tomorrow and never did another movie, it's a way for my family, my nieces, the younger kids in my family to see me and say, 'OK, that was Dolly the songwriter, that was Dolly the singer, that was Dolly the producer of the songs, that was Dolly the personality, Dolly the attitude, Dolly the values, the principles, the sense of humor,'" she explained. "It's just some of everything that I am, more than anything I've ever done."

How to watch: Straight Talk is available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

articles.body: Reactions and remembrances are pouring in following the death of Dolly Parton, the beloved country music icon, at age 80.Bryan Seaver, Parton's nephew and head of security for more than two decades, announced the news of her death on Instagram. A rep for the singer later issued a statement to People revealing that she had “bravely [faced] a brief battle with cancer.”"Dolly opened doors for singers, songwriters, musicians and dreamers from every walk of life," Seaver said. "By her example, we believed anything was possible.""She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD, and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not," he added. "Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever."Tributes poured in over the course of the day, with legends from the worlds of music, movies, TV and even politics sharing how much Parton inspired them with her talent, perseverance and, above all, her open heart. Parton's death comes after she announced in May that she was canceling her Las Vegas residency, which was set to begin in September after already being postponed nine months. She cited unspecified health issues but told the public in a video on Instagram that she was "responding really well to meds and treatments" and "improving every day."Follow below for updates, remembrances and more.
